newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas mixed late, fronts down on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas mixed late, fronts down on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures were mixed late Thursday in moderate trade, with front months still on the defensive from forecasts for more mild weather next week, industry sources said.
At 1445 EST, February was still 9.3 cents lower at $2.815 per million British thermal units, while March was down by 6.6 cents at $2.57. Others were mixed, with some late 1997s up.

"The values we've been trading at were predicated on good (Texas) intrastate demand, and when you don't have it, prices break below $3," said one Texas-based trader, noting Texas gas was showing up in Louisiana and pressuring the cash.
Despite Wednesday's AGA data showing an unexpectedly large 262 bcf weekly U.S. gas stock draw, traders said eastern inventories were still 19 percent over last year.
And with little extreme cold on the horizon, few expected much upside near term.

"This is a seasonal phenomenon. People think the critical time of winter has passed. We could see lows in the $2.40-2.60 range (basis February), but below $2.60, I think it's undervalued," said another Texas trader.

While cooler Midwest and Northeast weather was expected by the weekend, most regions were expected to warm to above-normal next week. And longer-term forecasts for February call for more normal to above-normal temperatures across most of the U.S, a factor undermining sentiment.

Technical traders, who said the five-day climb in open interest as prices moved lower was bearish, pegged key support in February at the December 31 low of $2.613. Psychological resistance was seen at $3.00, with better selling likely at $3.33, $3.64 and then $3.80-3.84.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were five to 10 cents lower Thursday in the $2.90-2.95 area. Midcon pipes were down by about a nickel to $2.80-2.85. New York city gate gas slipped five cents or more to about the $3.30 level.
NYMEX said 32,695 Hub contracts traded at 1330 EST.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas expires next Monday.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1445 EST.
On the KCBT, February was 10.5 cents lower at $2.64, while deferreds were down by one to 13 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.2 cents to 17.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
